text.p: Rating Agency Malaysia Bhd (RAM) said on Wednesday that there were no changes to the assigned credit ratings of the DRB-Hicom group following the death of its chairman.
In a statement, RAM said there are currently five companies under the group which have been rated by the agency.
RAM said the agency received many queries on whether it would review the ratings of the companies within the group after the death of Yahaya Ahmad on Monday in a helicopter crash.
"RAM has reviewed the credit quality of the respective debt issues and is of the opinion that no changes to the assigned credit ratings are required," it said.

The companies with the outstanding debt issues are heavy industrial group Hicom Holdings Bhd, diversified Gadek Malaysia Bhd, real estate firm Hicom-Gamuda Development Sdn Bhd, commercial vehicle assembler United Straits Fuso Sdn Bhd and Kedah Cement Sdn Bhd.
Gadek's 750 million ringgit 2.0 percent guaranteed redeemable unsecured bonds (1996/2001) was given a rating of AA2(bg) by RAM.

Hicom-Gamuda has a 245 million ringgit guaranteed revolving underwritten facility (1996/2001) which was rated P1(bg). United Straits Fuso has a 50 million ringgit guaranteed revolving underwritten notes issuance facility (1995/2000) rated P1(bg).

"The ratings assigned to the debt issues of Gadek Malaysia Bhd, Hicom-Gamuda Development Sdn Bhd and United Straits Fuso Sdn Bhd reflect the respective ratings of the guarantor banks which have not changed," RAM said.
Hicom's 500 million ringgit murabahah notes issuance facility (1997/2002) was rated P2.

The rating of A2 assigned to Hicom's 950 million redeemable secured bonds reflects the security pledge of shares assigned to the bondholders. These shares include those of carmaker Perusahaan Otomobil Nasional Bhd and Kedah Cement Holdings Bhd, Kedah Cement's parent firm.

"RAM expects the fundamental strength of these companies to prevail in allowing Hicom to maintain the security pledge for the benefit of bondholders. Hicom's fundamental strength also justifies its stand alone P2 rating for the murabahah notes issuance facility," RAM said.
